title: The Ray flat
kicker: S02 / S07 / S17 / S26 — INTERIOR MASTER
subtitle: Bed-Stuy · front room and kitchen table
alt: A modest 1970s Brooklyn railroad-flat front room with a formica kitchen table, a sideboard with a framed photograph and a hallway door.
summary: Etta's front room is the film's moral centre: a small table she signs papers at, a sideboard with the family photographs, and the hallway the stretcher went down.
design: Camera at seated human height, deep focus, window with fire escape camera-right and the bedroom doorway camera-left. Overcast daylight plus one warm practical lamp.
continuity: The same table serves the death signature (S02), the envelope Corn paid for (S07), the tape playback (S17) and the copying session (S26). The biscuit tin and the funeral-home bill stay on the sideboard.

title: The stoop
subtitle: Bed-Stuy · brownstone steps, Halloween morning
alt: A worn brownstone stoop with an iron railing and a green front door, seen from across a narrow Brooklyn street on an overcast morning.
summary: The threshold Etta keeps crossing: Jack waits on it, the coroner's van pulls away from it, and the neighbourhood watches from behind its windows.
design: Wide establishing shot from across the street at human height. Keep the street, the kerb and the gutter in frame; the fire escape reads above the door.
continuity: A Halloween mask hangs from the fire escape. Jack spits shells into the gutter, then scrapes one off his shoe on the step. The coroner's van pulls away to frame left.

title: Bug's bedroom
subtitle: The tape is made here, twice
alt: A cramped teenage bedroom with a single bed, a chest of drawers covered in cassettes and loose tape, a gooseneck lamp and taped-up magazine clippings.
summary: The smallest room in the film and the one that wins it: every copy, splice and loop of Peanut's laugh is made on the floor of this bedroom.
design: Cramped, slightly low camera, deep focus. Razor blade, grease pencil, splicing tape and loose reels of tape must read on the chest of drawers.
continuity: Two shoebox recorders face each other on the floor joined by a cable. The final loop is fed through a pencil and back into a recorder, never a sampler.

title: The morgue counter
subtitle: City morgue · personal effects
alt: A green-tiled city morgue corridor with a high wooden service counter, a sliding glass partition and harsh overhead fluorescent light.
summary: Institutional, fluorescent and cold: the corridor where Peanut's effects are reduced to a list, and where the laundry receipt first surfaces.
design: Camera down the corridor at human height. Keep the swinging door, the counter, the chained pen and the rubber-stamped form in frame.
continuity: The effects list holds keys, a laundry receipt and one empty glassine bag. Jack stays behind the line Etta gave him, two steps back, for the whole scene.

title: Jack's office
subtitle: One room over a closed travel agency
alt: A shabby one-room private investigator's office with a battered desk, a green filing cabinet, a sticking sash window and a faded travel poster outside.
summary: A room above a business that failed: the window Peanut repaired still sticks, and Pike lets himself in to leave a reminder on the desk.
design: Camera in the doorway at human height, late-morning light through the window. Keep the desk, the filing cabinet and the half-open window in the same frame.
continuity: The glassine bag and the note WE KNOW WHAT YOU WERE sit on the desk. Jack wraps them together and locks them in a drawer; Pike closes the window on his way out.

title: Vetrano's coffee shop
subtitle: Espresso, framed handshakes, one envelope
alt: A small Italian-American coffee shop with a chrome espresso machine, framed photographs of men shaking hands and small marble-topped tables.
summary: Sal's shop is Corn's front room: the framed handshakes on the wall are the biography of every man who has ever been paid to look the other way.
design: Camera at human height, wide and deep. Keep the counter camera-left, the framed photographs on the back wall and the booth where Corn sits facing the door.
continuity: Corn sits alone with a ledger page turned face down and pushes an envelope across without a greeting. Jack leaves sunflower shells on the clean saucer.

title: The back office
subtitle: Where Corn's books are really kept
alt: A cramped back office with a scarred desk, a columnar accounts book, a fountain pen, a filing cabinet and a frosted-glass door to the shop.
summary: Vera's room. Six years of Corn's accounts were balanced at this desk, and the duplicate transfer slip was taken out of this drawer.
design: Camera in the doorway at human height. Keep the desk lamp, the ledger she is writing in and the drawer within the same frame.
continuity: Corn closes her pen in the ledger and bends the nib. When he leaves, Vera opens the drawer: a city seal on a duplicate transfer slip, which she keeps.

title: City property office
subtitle: Kellerman's floor · Friday and Saturday
alt: A drab municipal office with a heavy desk, a receipt book, an ink pad, grey filing cabinets and a frosted-glass partition onto a clerks' room.
summary: Paperwork as a weapon. Lot Thirteen is laundered here with a stamp, a seal and a signature, and undone here the next morning by an evidence bag.
design: Camera at human height, deep focus through the frosted partition so Nicky's sorting tables and rolling cart are visible behind Kellerman's desk.
continuity: The oversized wood-handled stamp and the ink-stained cuff belong to this desk. Saturday: the same stamp in a clear evidence bag, and a badge set down on the desk.

title: The church kitchen
subtitle: Sandwiches, a wall telephone, a pencilled note
alt: A church basement kitchen with a stainless-steel work table, loaves of bread, a coffee urn, a wall telephone and a cork noticeboard of schedules.
summary: The only place in the film that is unambiguously trying to feed people, and the switchboard the anonymous tip comes through.
design: Camera at human height, deep focus. Keep the wall telephone with its long cord, the bread knife and the sandwich line in the same frame.
continuity: The pencilled note reads LOT 13, WAREHOUSE 3, EIGHT O'CLOCK. Harriett finishes the sandwiches before she does anything else about it.

title: The church basement
subtitle: Folding chairs, no organ, no verdict promised
alt: A plain church basement with rows of folding chairs facing a trestle table, a wooden cross on the wall, a coffee urn and a cassette recorder.
summary: The trial the film actually gets: no organ, no verdict, just a mother with paper, a tape and a room full of witnesses who have to hear the names said aloud.
design: Camera from the back of the room at human height. Keep the trestle table, the cassette recorder and the back row where Pike sits in civilian clothes.
continuity: Etta lays a transfer slip beside Peanut's torn corner; the stamp impressions match. She gives the original ledger to the lawyer and keeps no set for herself alone.

title: The church yard
subtitle: Stone steps, a hearse at the kerb, dusk
alt: A small Brooklyn church yard at dusk with stone steps down to the sidewalk, a brick wall with a basement door, a chain-link fence and a lit lamppost.
summary: Where the Panthers load a hearse with blankets and a hand truck, and where Harriett settles accounts with Vera afterwards.
design: Camera across the street at human height. Keep the steps, the basement door and the kerb in frame so a hearse can park at the bottom of the steps.
continuity: Homemade Halloween costumes march past in S19. By S29 the same hearse carries a sealed load, and Dove's arm is in a sling.

title: The auction office
subtitle: Navy Yard surplus · Lot Thirteen
alt: A navy yard auction office with a grilled service window, a clerk's desk with a ledger and clipboard, auction catalogues and a warehouse bay of pinball machines beyond.
summary: Nicky's room. The whole conspiracy is visible here if you know to ask what a sealed lot actually contains.
design: Camera at human height facing the service window, deep focus through the doorway to the pinball machines and stacked chairs behind.
continuity: Jack slides the laundry receipt through the window. The clock on the wall matters: the auction is public until 7:45. Kellerman enters with the oversized stamp.

title: The navy yard gate
subtitle: Buyers, a guard, a boom barrier
alt: The Brooklyn Navy Yard pedestrian gate with a chain-link fence, a brick guardhouse, a raised boom barrier and a hand-lettered auction sign, low afternoon sun.
summary: The last ordinary place in the film: men arguing about how to get a pinball machine into a van, while Vera watches Jack from a parked car across the street.
design: Camera just inside the gate looking out at human height. Keep the queue line, the guardhouse window and the street beyond in the same frame.
continuity: Clutch argues with the guard about the legs of the machine he bought. Across the street a parked car watches Jack; when he catches the driver's eye, she drives away.

title: The pool hall
subtitle: Tick Lane plays alone
alt: A dim smoky pool hall with two green-baize tables under low hanging lamps, a cue rack, a cigarette burning in a glass ashtray and dark wood panelling.
summary: Tick's room: the only place he is ever alone with a cue, a cigarette and a secret he is paid to keep.
design: Camera at human height, deep focus, long shadows under the table lamps. Keep the ashtray ledge and the cue rack within reach of the near table.
continuity: A cigarette burns in the ashtray the whole scene. Jack spits sunflower shells into a second, empty ashtray. Tick removes one glove only after Jack has gone.

title: Pike's car
subtitle: Parked beneath the elevated tracks
alt: The front seat of an unmarked 1970s detective's sedan parked under elevated subway tracks, with a folded overcoat on the passenger seat and iron columns through the windscreen.
summary: A confessional with the door left open. Trains drown out half of what Pike says, which is the point.
design: Camera from the back seat at eye level. Both front seats, the windscreen and the iron columns must read; the passenger door stays open in the frame.
continuity: Pike produces a surveillance photograph of Jack outside the Ray apartment with Bug in the doorway behind him. Jack takes the photograph with him when he gets out.

title: The diner
subtitle: A booth, two coffees, the numbers
alt: A worn 1970s diner booth with a Formica table, sugar shaker, ketchup and a napkin dispenser, a pastry case and a rain-streaked window onto a lit street.
summary: The exposition room that earns it: Vera keeps her coat on because she is not staying, and then tells Jack every number anyway.
design: Camera across the booth at human height. Keep the window, the coffee cup and the clear tabletop in frame; the waitress brings a plate for Jack's shells.
continuity: Vera sits with her coat on. She gives Jack her duplicate transfer slip here; its seal matches Peanut's torn corner.

title: Vera's car
subtitle: A red light she does not move on
alt: The front seat of a tidy mid-1970s compact sedan at night with papers and a slim ledger on the passenger seat and a red traffic light through the windscreen.
summary: The film's hardest conversation: a car idling at a green light because Vera will not drive on until she has been told what she did.
design: Camera from the rear passenger side at eye level. Both front seats, the red light ahead and the passenger door frame must read in the same frame.
continuity: The duplicate slip carries a telephone number in Vera's handwriting. Vera pulls into a space hard; Jack catches himself on the dashboard.

title: The payphone
subtitle: Coins, a ringing line, a warning
alt: A chrome wall payphone on a brick shopfront at night with a coin slot, a hood light, a newspaper box and wet pavement reflecting a streetlamp.
summary: The last chance to warn anyone, and it rings one ring too late: the Panthers left five minutes ago.
design: Camera a few feet back at human height, framing wide enough for two people to stand at the phone. Keep the handset, the coin slot and the hood light in frame.
continuity: Vera feeds coins; Jack stands close enough to hear the ring, not close enough to take the receiver. He takes the number and puts it in his pocket.

title: Warehouse 3
subtitle: Brooklyn Navy Yard · Friday night, after eight
alt: A vast navy yard warehouse bay at night with sodium lamps, a row of glowing pinball machines, stacked chairs, a seized Cadillac, a folding table with a receipt book and a big rolling bay door.
summary: The whole film arrives in this room. Sixty of its seventy-six beats happen under these sodium lamps, in front of forty pinball machines and a wall clock that reads 8:11.
design: Camera at human height from the middle of the floor, very wide. The bay door, the pinball row, the folding table with the stamp, the sealed cart and the cars must all read in one frame.
continuity: Clock over the bay door shows 8:11 when the Panthers come in. Nicky's cart holds the ledger; Kellerman's stamp and receipt book sit on the folding table; Clutch's Bally Spirit of '76 stands on a dolly.

title: The clinic
subtitle: Neighbourhood clinic · Friday night
alt: A small clinic treatment room with an examination table, a stainless-steel instrument tray, a gooseneck lamp, a glass-fronted supply cabinet and pale green walls.
summary: The morning after, at night: a nurse, a table and the first honest accounting of what the tourniquet cost.
design: Camera at human height, harsh small-practical fluorescent light. Keep the table, the instrument tray and the doorway to the corridor in the same frame.
continuity: A brown grocery bag with the ledger sits beneath Vera's chair; her hands are stained to the wrist. Jack's trouser leg is cut open.
